title: Modal Verbs: Obligation, Advice and Deduction
summary: Distinguish necessity, recommendation, prohibition and degrees of certainty.
learningObjectives: Use must, have to, should and must not appropriately.
Differentiate must not and do not have to.

explanation.heading: Necessity and rules
explanation.body: Must often expresses strong necessity or the speaker’s view; have to frequently reflects an external requirement.
explanation.example: You must wear eye protection. / Visitors have to register.

explanation.heading: No obligation vs prohibition
explanation.body: Do not have to means optional; must not means forbidden.
explanation.example: You do not have to attend. / You must not enter.

explanation.heading: Deduction
explanation.body: Must suggests a strong inference; might suggests possibility; cannot suggests a strong negative inference.
explanation.example: The lights are on: someone must be inside.

left.label: Do not have to
left.example: You do not have to print the report.

right.label: Must not
right.example: You must not share the password.

examples.sentence: You should check the power supply.

examples.note: A possible explanation, not a certainty.

examples.sentence: That cannot be the correct pinout.

commonMistakes.incorrect: You must not come tomorrow if you are busy.
commonMistakes.correct: You do not have to come tomorrow if you are busy.
commonMistakes.why: Must not expresses prohibition, not optional attendance.
Core modal auxiliaries take a bare infinitive.

studyTips: Use context to separate rules, advice and inference.
Remember that have to behaves like an ordinary verb in negatives and questions.

exercises.prompt: Access is prohibited. You ___ enter this room.
Attendance is optional. You ___ join the meeting.
exercises.feedback: Do not have to means there is no obligation.

exercises.prompt: The lights are on and I hear voices. Someone ___ be inside.
exercises.feedback: Must can express a strong deduction.

exercises.prompt: You look exhausted. You ___ take a break.
For safety reasons, you ___ (not / touch) the exposed terminals.
exercises.feedback: This is a prohibition: must not + base verb.

exercises.prompt: You ___ (not / have) to print this; a PDF is fine.
exercises.feedback: No obligation uses do not have to.

exercises.prompt: He ___ (be) at home: his car is outside and the lights are on.
exercises.feedback: Must + bare infinitive expresses a strong inference.

exercises.prompt: She ___ (should / check) the wiring before powering it up.
Correct the sentence: You must to wear safety glasses.
exercises.feedback: Do not use to after must.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: We do not must send the invoice today; it is optional.
acceptedAnswers: We don't have to send the invoice today; it is optional.
We do not have to send the invoice today; it is optional.
exercises.feedback: Use do not have to for lack of necessity.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: He should to restart the device.
Correct the sentence: You must not attend; it is optional.
acceptedAnswers: You don't have to attend; it is optional.
You do not have to attend; it is optional.
exercises.feedback: Optional means not required, not prohibited.
